warning: Post-hoc paper gate and correlated event rows: bound is illustrative, not a certified deployment guarantee.

sample_size_interpretation.method: Exact binomial inversion / one-sided Clopper-Pearson upper bound
sample_size_interpretation.unit: independent accepted evaluation case, not every incoming or correlated market row
sample_size_interpretation.limitations: Conditional on realized error count; fixed gate; no threshold search or multiple-look correction; not power for coverage uplift.
sample_size_interpretation.incoming_sample_conversion: n_accepted / coverage is an expectation for planning, not a guarantee of enough accepted cases.

cost_assumptions.status: illustrative assumptions, not measured market costs

uma_proposer_economics.role: Private expected profit of a proposer; separate from operator/human replacement cost and user settlement harm.
uma_proposer_economics.documented_context: Polymarket documents a typical $750 pUSD bond, return plus a reward when correct and undisputed, and loss for an incorrect or premature proposal. The adapter stores reward per market.
uma_proposer_economics.reward_status: $5 and $2 are sensitivity assumptions; no universal/current fixed proposal reward was verified. Read request-specific bond, currency and reward before any live evaluation.
uma_proposer_economics.break_even_formula: epsilon_star = (R-c)/(B+R), requiring R>c for positive tolerance
strong_assumptions: Every wrong or premature proposal is rejected and loses the entire bond B.
Every correct proposal returns the bond and earns R; dispute windfalls and failures are ignored.
c is the all-in per-proposal cost, including any gas, inference, search, capital lockup and operations counted in the scenario.
The reward and bond are expressed in comparable USD-equivalent amounts; token/depeg risk is ignored.
Equating the reported dataset error rate with rejected-proposal probability is illustrative only and is not empirically established.
uma_proposer_economics.excluded_claim: Proposer profit does not certify settlement accuracy, social welfare, or attacker resistance; bond is not the full loss per incorrect payout.
